docs.title: BLE flow diagrams — how far it runs, which files it goes through
docs.text:
Read this file before opening the code. Every diagram gives file:line → open the file next to it to compare. Covers all of Day 1 → Day 4 and both platforms (🤖 Kotlin · 🍎 Swift). Numbering: BLE Day 1 → Day 4 here = Day 06 → Day 09 of the curriculum (Week 2). Goal: once you can redraw diagram 3 (pipeline) and diagram 7 (state machine) with your eyes closed, then read the code in detail.

Path abbreviations used in this file:

  • 🤖 A/ = native-device-monitor/android/app/src/main/java/com/learn/nativedevicemonitor/
  • 🍎 I/ = native-device-monitor/ios/NativeDeviceMonitor/

docs.text:
🤖 ANDROID                                             🍎 iOS
 [Request] on PermissionScreen                          [Request] on PermissionView
      │                                                      │
      ▼                                                      ▼
 MainActivity.requestGroup :185                        PermissionService.request :116
      │ markAsked(group)    ← SharedPreferences flag         │
      │ requestPermissions.launch(SCAN + CONNECT) :89        ▼
      │  (API ≤ 30: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION)              requestBluetooth :147
      ▼                                                      │ authorization != .notDetermined? → return

      │                                                      ▼
      ▼                                                BluetoothPermissionProbe :179

      │ a Boolean is NOT ENOUGH to tell DENIED from PERMANENT│ wait for centralManagerDidUpdateState ≠ unknown
      ▼                                                      │ resume the continuation exactly once

      │ statusOf :57                                   refreshAll → CBManager.authorization

docs.title: 5. Day 1 — radio → Ready to scan
docs.text:
readiness(radio, permissionGranted)       🤖 BluetoothService.kt:67 · 🍎 BluetoothService.swift:67
      │
      ├─ radio == UNSUPPORTED ?  ──yes──► UNSUPPORTED        (🍎 the Simulator always lands here)
      │
      ├─ missing permission ?    ──yes──► MISSING_PERMISSION  → "Not ready" card + [Open Permissions]
      │   (🍎 also radio == .unauthorized)
      │
      ├─ radio != ON ?           ──yes──► RADIO_OFF           → 🤖 [Turn on] = ACTION_REQUEST_ENABLE
      │                                                          🍎 showSystemPowerAlert (only points the way)
      └─ otherwise ────────────────────► READY  ✅            → [Scan] button lights up

The radio changes live without leaving the screen:

  • 🤖 BroadcastReceiver ACTION_STATE_CHANGED registered in onStart (MainActivity.kt:231); radio OFF also calls bleClient.onRadioOff() (:233) → see §12 path C.
  • 🍎 RadioObserver.centralManagerDidUpdateState (BluetoothService.swift:104). The manager is only created after permission is granted (:55) — creating it earlier makes iOS show the permission dialog as soon as the screen opens.

docs.title: 6. Day 2 — scan → one advertising packet becomes one list row
docs.text:
[Scan]  🤖 ScannerScreen.kt:247  ·  🍎 ScannerView.swift:198
    │
    ▼
 startScan(filter)                          🤖 :320                         🍎 :144
    ├─ already scanning? → return            ✓                                ✓
    ├─ 🤖 scanner == null → "Bluetooth is off"   🍎 central.state != .poweredOn → return (trap 3)
    ├─ clear found / hidden / packetStats, devices = []
    │   🍎 keep the connected peripheral (trap 1: dropping the strong ref = connection dies silently) :159
    ├─ 🤖 scanner.startScan(scanCallback)   — ONE callback for the service's whole life :199
    │   🍎 scanForPeripherals(nil, AllowDuplicates: true) :171
    └─ schedule 10 s → stopScan()             → §13
         │
         ▼   (every advertising packet — dozens of times per second per device)
 🤖 onScanResult :201  (Binder thread)        🍎 didDiscover → handleDiscovered :309  (main)
    │
    ├─ name = device.name ?? the name in the advertising packet
    ├─ filter.matches(name)?  (BluetoothScanFilter — CarMD2 / CMD-*)
    │     └─ no → hidden.add(id) → hiddenCount   ("N other devices hidden")
    ├─ info = BluetoothDeviceInfo(id, name, rssi, advertisementOf(...))
    ├─ found[id] = info          ← overwrite = DEDUPE + RSSI always the latest
    │     🤖 id = MAC (LinkedHashMap keeps order)   🍎 id = UUID specific to this phone (+ an order array)
    └─ devices = a NEW list  (🤖 StateFlow compares with equals — mutating in place won't redraw the UI)
         │
         ▼
 UI: devices.filter { isDeviceShown(it, query, hideUnknown, hideAudio, selected, connected) }
         │   Device Name box · Hide unknown · Hide audio — filters the EXISTING list, no rescan
         │   the selected / connected device is always kept
         ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ ((•)) CMD-Test          ▂▄▆  -52 dBm   CONNECTABLE   │  ← tap = select
 │ ((•)) Unknown device    ▂▄   -71 dBm                 │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          [ Connect ]  [ Disconnect ]    ← scannerButtonsOf(hasSelection, connection, ready)

List order = first-seen order, not sorted by RSSI — sorting by signal makes rows jump around and you tap the wrong device (BluetoothClientService.swift:376). Name/audio filters: task 002 · bluetooth-audio-devices.md.

docs.title: 7. State machine — BluetoothConnectionState
docs.text:
🤖 A/nativecore/bluetooth/BluetoothDeviceInfo.kt:101 · 🍎 I/NativeCore/Bluetooth/BluetoothDeviceInfo.swift:76

                         connect(device)
     ┌──────┐  ───────────────────────────────►  ┌────────────┐
     │ Idle │                                     │ Connecting │ ── 🍎 not done in 15 s ─┐
     └──────┘                  ┌────────────────► └─────┬──────┘                         │
                               │ connect(another device)│ 🤖 STATE_CONNECTED             │
                               │ (old one cancelled first)│ 🍎 didConnect                │
                               │                        ▼                               │
     ┌──────────────┐          │               ┌─────────────────┐                      │
     │ Disconnected │ ◄────────┼────────────── │ Connected(name) │                      │
     │   (grey)     │  disconnect() manual     └────────┬────────┘                      │
     └──────┬───────┘          │                        │ signal lost · peripheral drops │
            │                  │                        │ radio off                     │
            │ connect()        │                        ▼                               │
            └──────────────────┤               ┌─────────────────┐ ◄────────────────────┘
                               └───────────────│  Error(message) │ ◄── 🍎 didFailToConnect
                                   connect()   │     (red)       │ ◄── 🤖 status=133 …
                                               └─────────────────┘

Telling manual from signal lost — both arrive on the same callback → the userRequestedDisconnect flag, set BEFORE calling disconnect (🤖 :461 · 🍎 :228). Set it after and an early callback reads the old flag → misreports "Unexpected".

docs.title: 8. Day 2 — sequence after tapping Connect
docs.text:
User         ScannerScreen/View        BluetoothClientService              OS stack        Peripheral
  │ tap a row       │                          │                               │                 │
  │────────────────►│ selected = device        │                               │                 │
  │ [Connect]       │                          │                               │                 │
  │────────────────►│─ connect(device) ───────►│ stopScan()                    │                 │
  │                 │                          │ old device? → cancel it       │                 │
  │                 │                          │ clearGattState · received = []│                 │
  │                 │                          │ userRequestedDisconnect=false │                 │
  │                 │ ◄── Connecting (spinner) │ 🍎 connectedPeripheral = p (trap 1)             │
  │                 │                          │ 🤖 gatt = connectGatt(ctx, false, cb, LE) :474  │
  │                 │                          │ 🍎 central.connect(p) :213 + 15 s timer        │
  │                 │                          │──────────────────────────────►│── CONNECT_REQ ─►│
  │                 │                          │                               │◄──── OK ────────│
  │                 │                          │ 🤖 onConnectionStateChange :345 (Binder)         │
  │                 │                          │ 🍎 didConnect → handleConnected :366 (main)     │
  │                 │                          │   callback from the OLD device? → ignore         │
  │                 │                          │   (🤖 g !== gatt · 🍎 isCurrent)                 │
  │                 │ ◄── Connected(name) 🟢   │ 🍎 cancel the 15 s timer                         │
  │                 │                          │ ──► startDiscovery  (Day 3, §9) — automatic     │
  • 🤖 autoConnect = false → connect right away, the OS gives up after ~30 s. TRANSPORT_LE stops dual-mode devices from picking Classic by mistake → 133.
  • 🤖 DISCONNECTED always gatt.close() (:372) — no close leaks a slot, the next connect returns status=133.

docs.title: 11. Day 4 — notify: CCCD 2902 → Received Data
docs.text:
Notify = the peripheral pushes data by itself when the value changes. The switch lives on the peripheral: descriptor CCCD 2902. Longer explanation: How to implement §6.0.

 [Notify] → onNotify(info, true)
      │
      │ 🤖 setNotify :536 — 2 STEPS, miss either and it's silent    🍎 setNotify :251 — 1 CALL
      │   c.getDescriptor(2902) == null → gattError "no CCCD"       peripheral.setNotifyValue(true, for: ch)
      │   ① setCharacteristicNotification(c, true)  ← local          (iOS writes the CCCD itself)
      │   ② enqueue writeDescriptor(2902 = 01 00 | 02 00)                 │
      │        (notify)   (indicate)                                      │
      │        │                                                          ▼
      │        ▼                                                   didUpdateNotificationStateFor
      │   onDescriptorWrite → handleCccdWritten :561                 → handleNotificationState :463
      │     error → undo step ① + gattError                           error → gattError
      │     OK    → markNotifying(key, true)                           takes the REAL ch.isNotifying
      └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                                     ▼
                  [Notify] button → [Stop] (blue) · lastEvent "Notify ON: FFE1"
                                     │
     ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ the peripheral pushes packets (every time the value changes) ─ ─ ─ ─ ─
                                     │
 🤖 onCharacteristicChanged :423 / :429           🍎 didUpdateValueFor → handleValue :498
    → handleNotified :575                              key NOT in pendingReads → NOTIFY
                                     │
                                     ▼
 GattValue(source = NOTIFY) → received = appendCapped(received, value)   (max 50, oldest pushed out)
                                     │    data → event → UI
                                     ▼
 ReceivedDataSection (🤖 GattSection.kt:312 · 🍎 GattSection.swift:262)

docs.title: 6.0 How notify works (read before 6.1)
docs.text:
The idea in one sentence: Read = the app asks and the peripheral answers once (pull). Notify = the app subscribes once, and from then on the peripheral pushes by itself whenever the value changes (push) — like subscribing to SMS alerts instead of phoning every second to ask. No "ask" packets, no polling lag, and the peripheral can sleep when there's nothing new.

All 3 pieces are needed — miss any one and it's silent, no error:

# Piece Where it lives Who handles it 1 The characteristic has the NOTIFY or INDICATE property peripheral (declared in its GATT) readable after discovery → the Notify button only shows when present (GattSection) 2 Descriptor CCCD 2902 = the "switch" on the peripheral: 01 00 notify · 02 00 indicate · 00 00 off peripheral the app writes it → only then does the peripheral start pushing 3 The phone's OS agrees to route packets to the app phone 🤖 setCharacteristicNotification(c, true) · 🍎 CoreBluetooth does it itself

What goes over the air (ATT — the layer below GATT):

 App (UI → Service)           OS Bluetooth stack                 Peripheral (dongle / ESP32 / nRF)
 ──────────────────           ──────────────────                 ─────────────────────────────────
 [Notify] tapped
   │ 🤖 setCharacteristicNotification(c,true) ─► (piece 3: "packets for c go to this app")
   │ 🤖 writeDescriptor(2902, 01 00)  ┐
   │ 🍎 setNotifyValue(true, ch) ─────┴──────► ATT Write Request  (CCCD handle = 01 00) ──►  CCCD := notify
   │                                         ◄── ATT Write Response (ok / error) ◄──────────┘
   │ 🤖 onDescriptorWrite(status) · 🍎 didUpdateNotificationStateFor(error)
   ▼ isNotifying = true → [Stop] button
                                                                  value changes (counter ticks, OBD answers…)
                                         ◄── ATT Handle Value Notification (handle, bytes) ── repeats forever
   🤖 onCharacteristicChanged(c, bytes) ◄──┘   (NO acknowledgement goes back)
   🍎 didUpdateValueFor(ch)            ◄──┘
   └─► GattValue(NOTIFY) ─► received (≤ 50) ─► ReceivedDataSection draws a new line

 [Stop] = exactly the same but writes CCCD 00 00 (🤖 write + setCharacteristicNotification(false) · 🍎 setNotifyValue(false))

Notify vs Indicate — the code picks automatically from the property (BluetoothClientService.kt:585; 🍎 CoreBluetooth picks itself):

Notify (01 00) Indicate (02 00) Acknowledgement none — fire and forget every packet needs a Confirmation from the phone (the OS sends it, the app does nothing) Speed fast, several packets per connection interval slow: the next packet waits for the previous confirmation Packet loss possible (weak signal, app too slow) no loss (the link layer retransmits) Typical use sensor streams, ESP32 counters, the dongle's UART FFE1 important events (Service Changed 2A05, commands that must arrive)

The subscription lifetime — tied to one connection, not to the app:

  • Disconnect (manual / signal lost / radio off) → the subscription is gone. An unbonded peripheral resets CCCD to 00 00; the next connection must discover again and tap Notify again (auto-resubscribe not done yet — §8.5 item 1).
  • A bonded peripheral remembers CCCD across connections → you should write 00 00 before disconnecting; the current version only turns it off on the OS side (BluetoothClientService.kt:485).
  • BluetoothGattCharacteristic / CBCharacteristic handles die with the connection → that's why every disconnect path calls clearGattState() (§6.3).
  • 🍎 The app goes to the background without UIBackgroundModes = bluetooth-central → iOS stops delivering packets; 🤖 keeps going until the process is killed (foreground service is Week 3).

The path of one packet through the code (data → event → UI):

Step 🤖 Android 🍎 iOS Packet arrives (BLE stack thread) :423 onCharacteristicChanged(g, c, value) (API 33+) · :429 the old variant must c.value.copyOf() immediately :648 didUpdateValueFor Tell read from notify 2 different callbacks → not needed shared callback with read → :498 handleValue: key in pendingReads = READ, otherwise NOTIFY Back to the main thread scope.launch { } (scope = Main) @MainActor class Bytes → value valueOf(c, bytes, NOTIFY) → BluetoothDecoder.decode (§5.2) same as 🤖 Store (keep the latest 50 lines) :608 handleNotified → appendCapped → _received: StateFlow :518 received = appendCapped(…) (@Observable) Draw collectAsState() → ReceivedDataSection ReceivedDataSection redraws by itself

Limits to know:

  • Default MTU is 23 → each notify packet carries at most 20 bytes of data; anything longer the peripheral sends is truncated. Task 004: 🤖 requestMtu(247) after discovery, 🍎 iOS negotiates itself; the GATT block shows MTU … · max … bytes per packet (§8.4).
  • Throughput is capped by the connection interval (usually 15–50 ms) × packets per interval; if the ESP32 pushes faster than that, notify packets are dropped and nobody reports it.
  • CarMD dongle: FFE1 is a UART port — enabling notify succeeds but no packets arrive until the app writes a command (ATZ\r, 010C\r…) into it; only then does the dongle's answer come back via notify. So for the dongle: Notify = the ears, Write = the mouth — Day 4 has the ears, task 004 adds the mouth (§8.4).

Tapped Notify but no lines appear — check in this order:

  1. Did the button turn into Stop? No → subscribe failed, read the red text (has no CCCD / status=…) — piece 2 is missing.
  2. It's Stop but still empty → is the peripheral really changing the value? (The nRF server must press send; the dongle must receive a written command first.)
  3. Logs: 🤖 adb logcat -s BleClient look for NOTIFY · 🍎 console [BleClient]. Log present but UI empty → a UI-layer bug; no log → packets never reach the app.
  4. Just reconnected? → the old subscription is gone, tap Notify again.

docs.title: 6.1 Flow
docs.text:
[Notify] on a characteristic with NOTIFY / INDICATE
   │  🤖 ① setCharacteristicNotification(c, true)        ← tells ANDROID to route packets to the app (local)
   │     ② enqueue { write CCCD 2902 = 01 00 (notify) | 02 00 (indicate) }   ← tells the PERIPHERAL to start pushing
   │  🍎 peripheral.setNotifyValue(true, for: ch)        ← iOS does both ① and ②
   ▼
 🤖 onDescriptorWrite(status)                 🍎 didUpdateNotificationStateFor(error)

docs.text:
Code What it does What happens without it 🤖 BluetoothClientService.kt:569 setNotify — 2 steps enable locally + write CCCD 2902 missing ① → the peripheral pushes but Android drops it · missing ② → the peripheral pushes nothing. Both are silent 🤖 :690 writeDescriptor API 33+ writeDescriptor(d, value) · older: set d.value then write the old API on 33+ still works but is deprecated; the new API on older devices → NoSuchMethodError crash 🤖 :594 handleCccdWritten only flips isNotifying once the peripheral confirms; on error undoes step ① the UI shows Stop while no packets ever arrive 🍎 BluetoothClientService.swift:521 handleNotificationState takes the real ch.isNotifying from CoreBluetooth guessing from what we requested → wrong when the characteristic has no CCCD 🤖 :482 disconnect · 🍎 :227 disconnect turns notify off before disconnecting late packets slip into the log after Disconnect was tapped 🤖 :392 / :732 clearGattState · 🍎 :330 — called on every disconnect path (manual, signal lost, radio off, device switch, connect fail) clears services, the queue, pending CCCD writes the dead device's service list stays → tapping Read gives a confusing Not connected; a stuck queue → the next connection's ops never run appendCapped(…, max = 50) keeps the latest 50 lines an ESP32 pushing hundreds of packets/second → the list bloats, the UI slows down then freezes

docs.title: 7. How to test
docs.text: Setup: 2 phones — phone A runs Native Device Monitor, phone B runs nRF Connect → Advertiser (add an advertising packet with Complete Local Name, turn on Connectable). Emulators/Simulators have no Bluetooth → only the permission part + the "unsupported/not ready" branch can be tested there.

docs.title: 7.1 Set up phone B as the peripheral (iPhone + nRF Connect)
docs.text:
The short step-by-step version (nRF Connect Android GATT server · LightBlue · ESP32) + the Scan → Connect → Pair → Read → Notify checklist: peripheral-setup.md.

 iPhone B — nRF Connect                          Android A — Native Device Monitor
 Advertiser ON (app in foreground)               Scanner tab, filter OFF
   Local Name "CMD-Test" + UUID 180D   ──BLE──►  row "CMD-Test" (strongest RSSI)
  1. iPhone B: turn Bluetooth on in Settings (the Control Center toggle may not fully turn it on).
  2. Open nRF Connect for Mobile → Advertiser tab → +.
  3. Use a short Local Name, e.g. CMD-Test. A name with the CMD- prefix is visible whether CarMD tools only is on or off, so it also works for case 12.
  4. Add a 16-bit Service UUID, e.g. 180D (Heart Rate) or 180F (Battery). Don't use a 128-bit UUID the first time.
  5. Turn Connectable on (only case 14 turns it off) → Save → turn on the toggle of the advertiser.
  6. Keep nRF Connect in the foreground with the screen on for the whole test.

Why it must be done exactly like this:

Point Reason The app must be in the foreground iOS drops the Local Name when the app goes to the background, and the Service UUID moves into an "overflow" area only other iPhones can read → Android sees nothing Short name, 16-bit UUID an advertising packet is only 31 bytes; a 128-bit UUID alone takes 18 bytes → the name gets truncated or pushed into the scan response Don't filter by MAC iPhones use a random address that rotates periodically → the MAC differs every test The name may not be CMD-Test 🤖 the code reads device.name first, then scanRecord.deviceName (BluetoothClientService.kt:223). If Android was ever paired with that iPhone it shows the system name ("…'s iPhone"); the first packet without a scan response shows Unknown. Look for the strongest RSSI

Phone A (Android) needs:

  • Bluetooth on. Android 12+ (API 31+): grant the Nearby devices permission. Android ≤ 11: also turn on Location (the system switch) + grant location permission, otherwise scanning returns 0 results with no error.
  • Scanner tab: CarMD tools only off (unless the name has CMD-), the Device Name box empty.
  • Keep the 2 phones close together.

Can't see it? Narrow it down in this order:

  1. Install nRF Connect on Android A → Scanner, no filters → does it see iPhone B? No = the problem is on iPhone B or phone A's permissions/Location, not the app.
  2. nRF on Android sees it but the app doesn't → send the adb logcat -s BleClient log (it has a startScan filter=... line) to check which filter is on.

Phone B can also be Android: nRF Connect Android → Advertiser tab → create a packet with Complete Local Name. Android has no foreground restriction like iOS.

 [Write] on a characteristic row ─► pick the write target (default writeTargetOf: FFE1 → Nordic RX 6E400002 → the first writable one ★)

    ├─ Invalid("21 bytes > max 20 for MTU 23")  → red text, Send dimmed
    └─ Ok(41 54 5A 0D, withResponse = has WRITE?) → preview "→ 41 54 5A 0D (4 bytes)"
    │
 [Send] ─► service.write(chr, bytes, withResponse)
    🤖 gattOps ─► writeCharacteristic(DEFAULT | NO_RESPONSE) ─► onCharacteristicWrite(status) ─┐
    🍎 writeValue(.withResponse)    ─► didWriteValueFor(error) ──────────────────────────────┤
       writeValue(.withoutResponse) ─► (iOS does NOT call back) ── log right away ───────────┤
                                                                                              ▼
                                            received += WRITE FFE1  41 54 5A 0D → "ATZ\r"
 ELM327 dongle runs the command ─► answers via notify FFE1 ─► received += NOTIFY FFE1  45 4C … → "ELM327 v1.5\r\r>"

 MTU
 🤖 discovery done ─► gattOps "Request MTU" ─► requestMtu(247) ─► onMtuChanged(mtu, status) ─► mtu
 🍎 didConnect + discovery done ─► maximumWriteValueLength(.withoutResponse) + 3 ─► mtu    (iOS negotiates itself)
 disconnect / switch device ─► clearGattState() ─► mtu = 23
Task 🤖 Android 🍎 iOS Send button rules GattModel.kt:191 planWrite GattModel.swift:179 planWrite Send :626 write — queued in gattOps like Read / CCCD :280 write — CoreBluetooth queues itself Write result :640 handleWritten :542 handleWritten (with response only) MTU :534 request · :654 handleMtuChanged :310 refreshMtu

Things to remember - Pick the write type from the properties. Has WRITE → with response (the peripheral ACKs, real errors come back). Only WRITE NO RESP → without response. 🍎 with the wrong type CoreBluetooth drops the write and only prints a warning; 🤖 usually returns an error status. - Without response doesn't mean the peripheral received it. 🤖 onCharacteristicWrite still arrives but only means "pushed down the stack"; 🍎 there's no callback at all. To be sure → use with response, or wait for the answer via notify (dongle). - The write callback doesn't return the bytes. You must keep them yourself (pendingWrite 🤖 / pendingWrites[key] 🍎) to print the WRITE line in Received Data. - 🤖 MTU is a GATT op → goes through gattOps. Calling requestMtu while another op is running = returns false, op lost. onMtuChanged can also arrive when the peripheral requests it → only opDone() when the in-flight op really is Request MTU. - 🍎 you can't request an MTU. iOS negotiates on connect (usually 185 or more); the app only reads maximumWriteValueLength(for: .withoutResponse) = MTU − 3. Don't read the .withResponse variant — it returns 512 because iOS splits "long writes" itself. - Longer than MTU − 3 is blocked, no automatic splitting (see Out of scope in task 004). ELM327 commands are only a few bytes so it's enough. - ELM327 dongles need \r at the end of a command. Without 0x0D the dongle waits and never answers — that's why Text mode accepts the \r escape, and every preset includes \r.

docs.title: 9. Note: BLE object model (Day 1 exercise)
docs.text:
CENTRAL (this app: the phone)                 PERIPHERAL (dongle / ESP32 / nRF Advertiser)
  ─────────────────────────────                 ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  scan  ◄──────── advertising packet ────────── advertises: name, service UUID, manufacturer data
  connect ─────────────────────────────────────► GATT server
                                                 └─ Service  (UUID, e.g. 180F Battery / FFE0 dongle)
                                                     └─ Characteristic (UUID + properties)
                                                          ├─ value (bytes)
                                                          └─ Descriptor 2902 (CCCD: notify on/off)
  read   ──── ask once ───────────────────────►  value            (the central pulls)
  write  ──── send bytes ─────────────────────►  value            (with / without response)
  notify ◄─── peripheral pushes on change ─────  value            (CCCD must be enabled first)
  • Central / peripheral: a role during the connection, not a kind of device. The central scans + connects; the peripheral advertises + waits.
  • Service: a group of functionality (Battery, Heart Rate, the dongle's UART port). Characteristic: one data slot inside a service, whose properties say READ / WRITE / NOTIFY.
  • UUID: the name of a service/characteristic. 16-bit (180F) is a SIG standard = 0000180F-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB; 128-bit is self-assigned.
  • Read = pull once · Write = push down · Notify = the peripheral pushes up continuously, cheaper than polling.

docs.title: 10. Explained for beginners
docs.text:
PermissionStatus with 4 states (instead of Boolean granted) - What: tells apart never asked / granted / denied but can ask again / only Settings left. - Why: each state needs a different button. Collapse them into false → "Request" shows when the dialog is dead, the user taps, nothing happens, they think the app is broken. - Ref: Android — Request runtime permissions

The "asked" flag in SharedPreferences (Android only) - What: remembers which permissions the app has ever shown a dialog for. - Why: checkSelfPermission + shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale give exactly the same result for "fresh install" and "denied twice". Without the flag a fresh install already shows Open app settings. iOS has .notDetermined so it doesn't need one. - Ref: shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale

registerForActivityResult lives in the Activity - What: registers the launchers for requesting permissions / enabling Bluetooth. - Why: they must be registered before the Activity is STARTED; calling it in a Composable/on a button tap throws IllegalStateException. - Ref: Activity Result APIs

BluetoothService.readiness() — a pure function combining permissions + radio - What: returns one single answer can we scan yet / what's blocking. - Why: with permissions but the radio off, scanning returns 0 devices without an error. 2 screens share 1 function → no screen guesses differently. - Ref: Set up Bluetooth · CBManagerState

BroadcastReceiver(ACTION_STATE_CHANGED) 🤖 / delegate centralManagerDidUpdateState 🍎 - What: know immediately when the user toggles Bluetooth. - Why: pulling down Quick Settings doesn't take the Activity through onResume → without listening the screen is wrong. Register in onStart, unregister in onStop, or it leaks. - Ref: BluetoothAdapter.ACTION_STATE_CHANGED

StateFlow 🤖 / @Observable 🍎 in BluetoothClientService - What: the service holds state (devices, isScanning, connection), the screen collectAsState() / reads the property and redraws by itself. - Why: Android BLE callbacks run on a Binder thread — writing a plain variable that Compose reads is a cross-thread access. iOS uses queue: nil so the delegate is already on main. - Ref: StateFlow · Observation

10 s scan timeout + dedupe by id - What: stopScan by itself after 10 s; a Map id → device overwritten on every packet. - Why: every advertising packet = 1 callback (dozens per second). An endless scan drains the battery + Android silently blocks you when you start too often. - Ref: Find BLE devices · scanForPeripherals

connectGatt(..., autoConnect=false, ..., TRANSPORT_LE) + always close() 🤖 - What: connect right away over BLE; close GATT on disconnect. - Why: without TRANSPORT_LE dual-mode devices may go over Classic by mistake → 133. No close() → leaked client slots, after ~30 times every connect returns 133. - Ref: Connect to a GATT server

Keep a strong ref to CBPeripheral + your own 15 s timeout 🍎 - What: store the peripheral in a dictionary before connect; schedule a 15 s Task.sleep then cancelPeripheralConnection. - Why: CoreBluetooth holds it weakly → when the peripheral is released the connection is cancelled silently; iOS connect never times out by itself. - Ref: connect(_:options:)

scannerButtonsOf() / isDeviceShown() — screen rules are pure functions, not inside the Composable/View - What: scannerButtonsOf takes (selected?, connectable?, is it the connected device?, state, ready) and returns Connect enabled/disabled/spinner + Disconnect enabled/disabled; isDeviceShown decides which rows show based on the Device Name box + the 2 switches. - Why: many combinations make it easy to miss a case (e.g. right after Error Connect must work again; the connected device must never be hidden by a switch). Inside the UI it can only be checked by hand on a device; split out, the unit tests run in 1 second, and both platforms share the same cases. - Ref: Android — Guide to app architecture (UI layer) · Swift Testing

Ignore callbacks from the OLD connection when switching devices - What: connected to A, select B and tap Connect → A is dropped; a late "A disconnected" callback is ignored (🤖 g !== gatt · 🍎 compare peripheral.identifier). - Why: BLE callbacks arrive asynchronously. Without filtering, "A disconnected" arrives while B is Connecting… → the card flips to Disconnected, row B loses its spinner even though B is still connecting. - Ref: BluetoothGattCallback.onConnectionStateChange · didDisconnectPeripheral

The list keeps first-seen order, not sorted by RSSI - What: new rows are appended at the end; RSSI updates in place. - Why: tapping a row = selecting the device to Connect, so rows must not move — RSSI changes several times a second, sorting by signal means your finger lands on another device.

The screen's "clock": LaunchedEffect + delay(1000) 🤖 / TimelineView(.periodic) 🍎 - What: redraw every second so "Last seen: 3s ago" counts by itself and cards fade on their own. - Why: the UI only redraws when state changes. A silent device = no new packets = no new state → without a clock the card never fades when it should. - Ref: LaunchedEffect · TimelineView

The gattOps GATT queue (🤖 only) — Day 3 - What: each read / CCCD write is one GattOp; the next op only runs when the previous op's callback arrives (opDone()). - Why: the Android Bluetooth stack runs one GATT op at a time. Calling readCharacteristic while a descriptor write is in flight → returns false, the op is lost, no callback at all → the UI waits forever. CoreBluetooth queues by itself so 🍎 doesn't need it. - Ref: BluetoothGatt.readCharacteristic · Punch Through — Android BLE guide (operation queue)

Properties are a bitmask, GattProperties.of(raw) — Day 3 - What: 1 byte declared by the peripheral → 5 flags READ / WRITE / WRITE NO RESP / NOTIFY / INDICATE → decide which buttons show. - Why: Android's PROPERTY_* and iOS's CBCharacteristicProperties are the same bit values from the spec → 1 function, 1 test suite for both platforms. Showing a Read button for a non-READ characteristic = an error on tap. - Ref: BluetoothGattCharacteristic.PROPERTY_READ · CBCharacteristicProperties

Little-endian + decode by UUID — Day 3 - What: decode(uuid, bytes) — known UUID → per spec (battery %, UTF-8 strings, heart rate), unknown → ASCII / uint LE / hex only. - Why: BLE sends the low byte first: 34 12 = 0x1234 = 4660. Reading it backwards as 13330 is the most common hand-decoding bug. Kotlin's Byte is signed → always and 0xFF. - Ref: Bluetooth SIG — Assigned Numbers / GATT Specification Supplement

Read and notify arrive on the same callback (🍎) — Day 3–4 - What: pendingReads remembers the key just readValued; didUpdateValueFor with that key → READ, without → NOTIFY. - Why: CoreBluetooth doesn't say whether a value arrived because we asked or because the peripheral pushed. Android splits it into 2 callbacks (onCharacteristicRead / onCharacteristicChanged). - Ref: peripheral(_:didUpdateValueFor:error:)

CCCD 2902 — Day 4 - What: the "switch" descriptor on the peripheral; write 01 00 = notify on, 02 00 = indicate on, 00 00 = off. - Why: the peripheral pushes nothing until someone enables the CCCD. 🤖 must do 2 steps itself (setCharacteristicNotification + write CCCD), missing either is silent with no error. 🍎 setNotifyValue does both. - Ref: Android — Receive GATT notifications · setNotifyValue(_:for:)

API 33 callbacks (🤖) — override both the new and the old version — Day 3–4 - What: onCharacteristicRead(…, value, status) / onCharacteristicChanged(…, value) for API 33+; the old ones read c.value + copyOf() for API 26–32 (the old ones guard SDK_INT >= 33 → return). - Why: minSdk 26. Writing only the new version → Android 12 and below never get data. The old version uses one shared buffer c.value → the next notify packet overwrites the previous one unless copied immediately. - Ref: BluetoothGattCallback.onCharacteristicChanged

clearGattState() on every disconnect path + keep the log — Day 4 - What: manual disconnect, signal lost, radio off, device switch, connect fail all call one function that clears services + the queue + pending CCCD writes. received / lastRead are kept until Connect to a new device or Clear. - Why: characteristic objects die with the connection — keeping them means tapping Read on a dead object. The log is kept because it's exactly what you need to read after "killing the peripheral" to know what the last packet was.

appendCapped(…, 50) — Day 4 - What: append the new line at the end, drop the oldest when over 50. - Why: notify can be hundreds of packets/second (ESP32 BLE_notify); an unbounded list → memory + draw time grow forever, the screen freezes after a few minutes.

BluetoothConnectionState is a sealed interface / an enum with associated values - What: 5 states, Connected carries the name, Error carries the reason. - Why: exhaustive when / switch — add a state and forget to draw it in the UI → build error, not a runtime bug. Disconnected (we tapped, grey) is separate from Error (dropped, red). - Ref: Sealed classes · Swift enums

Write with response / without response — task 004 - What: planWrite picks the type from the properties: has WRITE → with response, only WRITE NO RESP → without response. - Why: with response = the peripheral sends an ACK → you know for sure it arrived, errors (e.g. not writable) come back for real. Without response is faster but "fire and forget": 🍎 no callback, 🤖 the callback only means it was sent. 🍎 writing with the wrong type for the properties silently drops the write. - Ref: BluetoothGatt.writeCharacteristic · CBCharacteristicWriteType

fromHex / fromText + the \r escape — task 004 - What: convert typed text into bytes. Hex accepts 41 54, 4154, 0x41,0x54; Text turns \r \n \t \\ into the real characters. - Why: the input box can't type Enter as 0x0D, yet ELM327 only runs a command when it sees \r. Many hex styles are accepted because people copy from nRF / Logcat / docs. Pure functions → the same test cases on both sides. - Ref: ELM327 datasheet — AT commands

MTU = the max ATT packet, data = MTU − 3 — task 004 - What: 🤖 requestMtu(247) through the queue after discovery, the real value arrives in onMtuChanged; 🍎 reads maximumWriteValueLength(for: .withoutResponse). The UI shows MTU · max bytes and blocks longer payloads. - Why: the default 23 → only 20 data bytes per packet (3 bytes opcode + handle). Longer notify / write packets get truncated or rejected (status=13 INVALID_ATTRIBUTE_LENGTH). The MTU belongs to one connection → back to 23 after a disconnect. - Ref: BluetoothGatt.requestMtu · maximumWriteValueLength(for:) · Punch Through — Maximizing BLE throughput

docs.title: How audio devices are detected
docs.text: ← How to implement §8.3

docs.title: Bluetooth audio devices — recognising headphones / speakers in a BLE scan
docs.text: Status: 🟡 coded 22/09 — 🤖 isAudioDevice() in ui/scanner/ScannerActions.kt (+ BluetoothDecoder.appearanceOf, tables in BluetoothLookup.kt) · 🍎 UI/Scanner/ScannerActions.swift. Unit tests pass; not yet surveyed in the field with real headphones (§4), so the set of signs may still need tuning.

docs.title: 1. Why headphones end up in the BLE scan list
docs.text:
AirPods / Galaxy Buds / JBL
   ├─ Bluetooth Classic (A2DP, HFP)  ── music + calls      ── does NOT show up in a BLE scan
   └─ BLE advertising                ── quick-pair popup, battery, Find My
                                         └─► the app's scan sees it ─► Scanner list full of headphones

Headphones really do send BLE packets, but they aren't BLE (GATT) devices this app needs to connect to → the Hide audio devices filter hides them so the CMD-… dongle is quicker to find. Classic-only headphones never show up in a BLE scan in the first place — no filtering needed.

docs.title: 2. How to recognise them
docs.text:
Before connecting, the app only has the advertising packet. No field says "I am headphones" → it has to be inferred from signs:

Sign What it is 🤖 🍎 Confidence Appearance (AD type 0x19) the device declares its type from the Bluetooth SIG code table: 0x0941 Earbud · 0x0942 Headset · 0x0943 Headphones · 0x084x Audio Sink (speaker) · 0x088x Audio Source ✅ read from scanRecord.bytes ❌ CoreBluetooth doesn't expose it the most reliable, but many vendors don't send it LE Audio service UUID 184E ASCS · 1850 PACS · 1853 CAP · 184F BASS — only LE Audio devices have them ✅ ✅ reliable, but few headphones support it yet Device class device.bluetoothClass.majorDeviceClass == AUDIO_VIDEO — the system knows it from a previous pairing / Classic scan ✅ ❌ reliable, but only for paired or dual-mode devices Google Fast Pair service data FE2C — Android earbuds (Pixel Buds, Sony, JBL…) advertise it for the quick-pair popup ✅ ✅ fairly reliable — trackers use it too; the code still hides a device with only FE2C (a tracker isn't a dongle either) Apple proximity pairing manufacturer 0x004C + type byte 0x07 — the packet that pops up AirPods on an iPhone ✅ ✅ fairly reliable for AirPods/Beats; derived from community reverse engineering, Apple doesn't publish it. (0x12 is Find My / AirTag — not audio) Name contains Buds, AirPods, JBL… guessing from the name ✅ ✅ weak — not used

docs.title: 3. Principles (applied in the code)
docs.text:
• There's no 100% reliable way. Headphones sending none of the signs above → the filter doesn't recognise them → they stay visible.
  • Better to miss one than wrongly hide a CMD-… dongle: hide only on a reliable sign; the Connected / selected device is never hidden.
  • 🍎 recognises fewer than 🤖 (no Appearance + device class) — stated plainly, no attempt to make both sides equal by guessing names.
  • Pure function isAudioDevice(adv) in ScannerActions.kt / ScannerActions.swift; Appearance / UUID code tables in BluetoothLookup; unit tests share the same cases on both platforms (🍎 skips the Appearance / device class cases).
  • Fast Pair FE2C on its own also counts as audio: trackers use FE2C too, but a tracker isn't a dongle either → wrongly hiding a tracker is fine.

docs.title: 4. Remaining work: field survey
docs.text:
Survey in the field to confirm / tune the rules: scan on the Samsung A32 (and an iPhone) next to a few real headphones — AirPods, Galaxy Buds, an Android headset with Fast Pair — record what Appearance / Service UUID / service data / manufacturer data each one sends, fill in the table below, then lock down the set of signs.

docs.title: Setting up a test peripheral — nRF Connect (+ LightBlue, ESP32)
docs.text: Phone A = the phone running Native Device Monitor (central). Phone B = the simulated peripheral. Button names in nRF Connect / LightBlue may differ slightly between versions — look for the meaning, not the exact words. Reasons + advertising troubleshooting in detail: How to implement §7.1 · the full list of test cases: §7.2.

docs.title: Which peripheral to pick
docs.text:
Phone B Scan / Connect Read Notify Use when Android + nRF Connect (Advertiser + Configure GATT server) ✅ ✅ value you set ✅ sent by hand recommended — covers the whole flow iPhone + nRF Connect (Advertiser only) ✅ ⚠️ only the iPhone's system services (180A → Apple Inc.) ❌ practically none Day 2 only (scan / connect) iPhone / Android + LightBlue → Virtual Devices ✅ ✅ ✅ no second Android available ESP32 + Arduino sketch BLE_notify ✅ ✅ ✅ pushes continuously dense streams, the 50 cap, pulling the plug

Prefer a Battery Service 180F → Battery Level 2A19 (READ + NOTIFY): the app picks it as both the Read target and the Notify target and decodes it as 90 % — correct at a glance.

docs.title: A. Android B + nRF Connect (recommended)
docs.text:
Step 1 — Create a GATT server (what phone A will read / subscribe to)

  1. Install nRF Connect for Mobile (Nordic) on phone B, turn Bluetooth on.
  2. Menu ☰ → Configure GATT server → add a server config (or edit the Sample configuration).
  3. Add service → pick the predefined Battery Service (180F).
  4. In that service, characteristic Battery Level (2A19): tick the Read + Notify properties, set the initial value to 5A (= 90). It comes with a CCCD 2902 descriptor — without it Notify reports red has no CCCD (case 24).
  5. (Optional, to test pairing) add another characteristic with permission Read encrypted / Read encrypted MITM.
  6. Save → select the new config as the active server.

Step 2 — Advertise so phone A can find it

  1. Advertiser tab → + → set a name, e.g. CMD-Test.
  2. Advertising data → Add record → Complete Local Name; add Service UUID 180F.
  3. Options: turn on Connectable · interval Low latency if available.
  4. Save → turn on the packet's toggle. Keep phone B's screen on.

docs.title: B. iPhone B + nRF Connect (Day 2 only)
docs.text: Advertiser tab → + → Local Name CMD-Test + Service UUID 180D → Connectable → turn on the toggle. Keep nRF Connect in the foreground — once iOS goes to the background it drops the Local Name and Android can't see it.

docs.title: C. LightBlue (iOS or Android, Punch Through)
docs.text:
1. Virtual Devices tab → + → pick the Heart Rate or Battery template → turn on the virtual device switch.
  2. Open the virtual device → tap a characteristic → edit the value (hex). Once phone A has subscribed, every edit = 1 notify packet.
  3. iPhone: LightBlue must also stay in the foreground.

docs.title: D. ESP32
docs.text: Arduino IDE → Examples → BLE → BLE_notify → flash. Service 4fafc201-…, characteristic beb5483e-… (READ · WRITE · NOTIFY · INDICATE), pushes a uint32 counter whenever a client subscribes. Nothing else to configure.

docs.title: 2. How connecting and working with it goes
docs.text:
Phone B (peripheral)                                Phone A — Native Device Monitor
 ────────────────────                                ──────────────────────────────
 Advertiser ON  ── advertising packet "CMD-Test" ──► Scan → row CMD-Test
 GATT server    ◄── Connect ──────────────────────── select row → [Connect]
                ── list of services ───────────────► Discover (automatic) → 180F / 2A19 ★ target
 2A19 = 5A      ◄── Read ─────────────────────────── [Read]  → value: 90 %
 CCCD 2902 = 01 ◄── write CCCD (subscribe) ───────── [Notify] → button becomes [Stop]
 edit 2A19 → 50 ── notification ───────────────────► Received Data: NOTIFY 2A19 … → 80 %
                ◄── write CCCD = 00 ──────────────── [Stop]
                ◄── Disconnect ───────────────────── [Disconnect] → grey Status
  • Connect only opens the link; the app does not pair by itself. Pairing (bonding) only happens when phone A touches a characteristic that requires encryption → the OS shows a pairing dialog.
  • Sending a notify from nRF Connect (Android B): once A is connected, nRF Connect on B shows an extra tab / screen for that client (the Server area) → pick Battery Level → the edit-value button (↑ arrow) → enter 50 → choose send notification (or tick notify then Send). Each send = 1 new line on A.
  • Phone A only receives notifications after tapping Notify; anything sent before that isn't pushed by the peripheral (CCCD is still 00 00).
  • Disconnecting = losing the subscription → after reconnecting you must tap Notify again. Why: §6.0.

docs.title: 3. Check along the flow: Scan → Connect → (Pair) → Read → Notify → Stop → Disconnect
docs.text:
On phone A keep CarMD tools only off and the Device Name box empty (or type cmd). Each step has exactly 1 correct result — if a step is wrong, stop at that step.

# Step (phone A) Phone A must show Phone B / notes §7.2 case 1 Scan row CMD-Test, RSSI changing constantly; stops by itself after 10 s not visible → B's Advertiser toggle isn't on / iPhone B isn't in the foreground 7 2 Tap the row → Connect spinner → CONNECTED tag + green dot Connected to CMD-Test nRF on B shows the newly connected client 8 3 (automatic) Discover Discovering services… → N services · M characteristics; row 2A19 labelled READ NOTIFY + ★ target 180F missing → B hasn't selected the right server config 19–20 4 Read 2A19 Last read raw: 5A · value: 90 % + 1 READ line change the value on B then Read again → new number 21 5 Pair (optional) — Read the encrypted characteristic the OS pairing dialog → Pair → Read succeeds tap Cancel → red text Read … failed, status=5/15 (🍎 insufficient authentication/encryption error), Status stays green 22 6 Notify 2A19 the button becomes a blue Stop · Notify ON: 2A19 red has no CCCD → 2902 missing in step 1A.4 23–24 7 B sends a notification (value 50, 3C…) 1 line per send HH:mm:ss.SSS NOTIFY 2A19 … → 80 %, counter N / 50 with an ESP32 lines flow continuously, capped at the latest 50 23 8 Stop Notify OFF: 2A19, the button back to Notify, further sends from B add no lines 25 8b (task 004) Write — needs a characteristic with the Write property (nRF: add a characteristic with Write ticked; ESP32 BLE_notify has one) the GATT block shows MTU … · max … bytes; tap Write on that row → Hex 01 02 → Send → line WRITE <uuid> 01 02 → 513 (uint16 LE) nRF on B sees the new value; no WRITE → no Write button 31–34 9 Disconnect grey Status Disconnected, GATT block empty, old log kept 9, 26 10 Connect again → turn off phone B's Advertiser / Bluetooth while notifying red Status Unexpected disconnect…, no crash, Connect works again ESP32: pull the plug 10, 27

Logs to compare: 🤖 adb logcat -s BleClient · 🍎 Xcode console filtered on [BleClient]. Unpair after testing: Settings → Bluetooth on both phones → Forget / Unpair CMD-Test (otherwise the dialog won't show next time).

docs.title: Build guide
docs.text:
Build one native app twice: Swift + SwiftUI for iOS and Kotlin + Jetpack Compose for Android, with no cross-platform layer in between.

The example app is Native Device Monitor. It has 5 tabs (Permissions · Scanner · Media · API · Monitor) and the code for both platforms lives in native-device-monitor/.

iOS 17+ · Swift 5 · SwiftUI Android 8.0+ (API 26) · Kotlin 2.4 · Compose Beginner friendly

docs.title: The path
docs.text: Step Page You finish with 1 Set up the tools Xcode, Android Studio, JDK 17, a simulator and an emulator that boot 2 One app, two codebases A map of which file does what, on both sides 3 Build & run on iOS The app on the Simulator and on your iPhone 4 Build & run on Android The app on the emulator and on your Android phone 5 Swift ↔ Kotlin side by side A cheat sheet for reading one codebase while writing the other 6 Feature by feature Permissions, BLE, media, HTTP, background: what differs and why 7 Test both apps Unit tests that run without a phone, same cases on both sides 8 Ship checklist Clean build, lint / analyze, end-to-end check on real devices

docs.title: How to use this guide
docs.text:
• Build each layer twice before moving on. Write the Swift version, then the Kotlin version of the same file. The second one goes fast, and the differences stick.
  • NativeCore first, UI second. A screen should only read state and call methods. If a View/Composable imports CoreBluetooth or BluetoothGatt, move that code down.
  • Run on a real phone for anything hardware. Simulators and emulators have no Bluetooth.

docs.title: 1 · Set up the tools
docs.text: One Mac runs both toolchains. Plan one evening; most of it is downloads.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: 🍎 iOS 🤖 Android IDE Xcode 16+ (the app is built with Xcode 26.5) Android Studio (AGP 8.13.2) Language / UI Swift 5 · SwiftUI · @Observable Kotlin 2.4 · Jetpack Compose (BOM 2026.06.01) · Material 3 Min OS iOS 17.0 Android 8.0 (API 26) · target 36 JDK — 17+ (21 recommended) Project generator XcodeGen (only to add/rename files) Gradle wrapper (./gradlew), already in the repo Real BLE Simulator has no Bluetooth → real iPhone Emulator has no Bluetooth → real Android phone Test peripheral nRF Connect for Mobile on a second phone, or an ESP32 same

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Xcode from the App Store, open it once and let it install the iOS platform and a Simulator. 
    xcode-select -p
    It should print a path inside Xcode.app. If it prints CommandLineTools, run sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app yourself.
  2. Install XcodeGen (you only need it when you add or rename Swift files): 
    brew install xcodegen
  3. Install Android Studio, then in SDK Manager install Android SDK Platform 36 and Build-Tools. Create an emulator in Device Manager (any Pixel image, API 34+).
  4. Check the JDK Gradle will use. Android Studio ships one; from the terminal: 
    java -version
    Anything from 17 up works. If Gradle sync complains about the JVM, set Settings → Build Tools → Gradle → Gradle JDK to the bundled JDK 21.
  5. Clone the repo: 
    git clone https://github.com/tucarmd/native-mobile-learning.git
  6. Turn on developer mode on your phones: iPhone Settings → Privacy & Security → Developer Mode; Android About phone → tap Build number 7 times → USB debugging.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• xcodebuild -version prints Xcode 16 or newer
  • xcrun simctl list devices booted shows a Simulator after you open one
  • adb devices lists your emulator or phone
  • Android Studio opens native-device-monitor/android/ and Gradle sync finishes

Common setup mistakes

  • SDK location not found: open the project once in Android Studio; it writes local.properties with sdk.dir=.... That file is per machine, don't commit it.
  • Incompatible Gradle JVM: the Gradle JDK is too new or too old. Pick the bundled JDK in Android Studio.
  • iPhone not visible in Xcode: unlock it, tap Trust, and enable Developer Mode (needs a restart).

docs.text:
1. Open the project 
    open ios/NativeDeviceMonitor.xcodeproj

docs.title: Example 1 · A closed set of results
docs.text:
The HTTP client never throws to the UI. It returns one of five cases, and the screen switches over them.

SwiftKotlin NativeCore/Network/ApiResult.swift
enum ApiResult: Equatable {
    case success(status: Int, body: String, contentType: String?, durationMs: Int)
    case httpError(status: Int, body: String, durationMs: Int)
    case timeout(seconds: Double, durationMs: Int)
    case noNetwork(message: String, durationMs: Int)
    case failure(message: String, durationMs: Int)
}
nativecore/network/ApiClient.kt
sealed interface ApiResult {
    val durationMs: Long

    data class Success(val status: Int, val body: String, val contentType: String?, override val durationMs: Long) : ApiResult
    data class HttpError(val status: Int, val body: String, override val durationMs: Long) : ApiResult
    data class Timeout(val timeoutMs: Int, override val durationMs: Long) : ApiResult
    data class NoNetwork(val message: String, override val durationMs: Long) : ApiResult
    data class Failure(val message: String, override val durationMs: Long) : ApiResult
}

Both are closed: add a case and the compiler points at every switch / when that forgot it.

docs.title: Example 2 · A pure function
docs.text:
Bytes from a Bluetooth characteristic → a readable value. No platform API, so it is the easiest kind of code to port and to test.

SwiftKotlin NativeCore/Bluetooth/BluetoothDecoder.swift
static func decode(_ uuid: String, _ data: Data) -> String {
    let bytes = [UInt8](data)
    guard !bytes.isEmpty else { return "(empty)" }
    switch uuid.uppercased() {
    case "2A19":
        return "\(bytes[0]) %"                       // battery level
    case _ where utf8Characteristics.contains(uuid.uppercased()):
        let text = String(decoding: bytes, as: UTF8.self)
        return String(text.reversed().drop(while: { $0 == "\u{0}" }).reversed())
    case "2A37":
        return heartRate(bytes)
    default:
        return guess(bytes)
    }
}
nativecore/bluetooth/BluetoothDecoder.kt
fun decode(uuid: String, bytes: ByteArray): String {
    if (bytes.isEmpty()) return "(empty)"
    return when (uuid.uppercase()) {
        "2A19" -> "${bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF} %"   // battery level
        in UTF8_CHARACTERISTICS -> bytes.toString(Charsets.UTF_8).trimEnd('\u0000')
        "2A37" -> heartRateOf(bytes)
        else -> guess(bytes)
    }
}

Bytes are signed in Kotlin

Byte in Kotlin is -128…127. Always mask with and 0xFF before treating it as a number. Swift's UInt8 is already 0…255.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Goal: check, request and react to the result for Bluetooth and Camera, including the denied paths.

🍎 iOS 🤖 Android Bluetooth permission one NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription API 31+: BLUETOOTH_SCAN + BLUETOOTH_CONNECT · API ≤ 30: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION States notDetermined · granted · denied · restricted NOT_REQUESTED · GRANTED · DENIED · PERMANENTLY_DENIED After a deny final at once → only Settings can ask again once → then permanently denied → Settings How you tell CBManager.authorization, AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus checkSelfPermission + shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale + an "asked before" flag

The bug to avoid

Collapsing every "not granted" into false. The user taps Request, no dialog appears (it's permanently denied), and they think the app is broken. A denied-for-good card must show Open Settings instead.

Code: PermissionService · PermissionStatus · PermissionGroup → task notes in HOW-TO §3.

docs.title: Scanner (Bluetooth LE)
docs.text:
Goal: scan (10 s timeout, no duplicates), filter by name, hide unnamed and audio devices, connect, discover GATT, read, notify, write.

🍎 iOS 🤖 Android Device id a UUID assigned by this iPhone MAC address, same on every phone Connect timeout waits forever → the app sets 15 s system gives up after ~30 s Discover two rounds: services, then characteristics per service discoverServices() returns both GATT operations CoreBluetooth queues them one at a time: the app keeps its own queue, otherwise calls return false and are lost Enable notify setNotifyValue(true, for:) setCharacteristicNotification and write the 2902 descriptor yourself Radio off while connected no didDisconnect → the app cleans up may not call back → the app cleans up

Code: BluetoothService (radio) · BluetoothClientService (scan, connect, GATT) · GattModel (pure rules) · BluetoothDecoder → tasks 001 · 002 · 003 · 004.

You need a second device to test this: Test peripheral setup.

docs.title: Media
docs.text:
Goal: take a photo or pick one, then show source · name · size · MIME · dimensions. Cancel is handled.

🍎 iOS 🤖 Android Camera UIImagePickerController wrapped for SwiftUI (CameraPicker.swift) ActivityResultContracts.TakePicture into a FileProvider URI Library PhotosPicker (no photo-library permission needed) Photo Picker (PickVisualMedia, no storage permission)

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Goal: GET / POST / HTTP 500 / timeout against jsonplaceholder and httpbin, buttons locked while a request runs.

🍎 iOS 🤖 Android Client ApiClient protocol with two backends: own URLSession code and Alamofire (switch on the API tab) ApiClient on HttpURLConnection Threading async / await suspend + withContext(Dispatchers.IO) Result enum ApiResult sealed interface ApiResult

docs.title: Monitor (background)

Goal: battery / network / Bluetooth status, a JSONL log file, and a monitor that keeps logging when the app is in the background.

🍎 iOS 🤖 Android In the foreground in-app loop in-app loop In the background BGAppRefreshTask (~30 s, when iOS decides) Foreground Service (dataSync, shows a notification) or WorkManager periodic job Setup UIBackgroundModes: fetch + BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC + POST_NOTIFICATIONS (API 33+) + foregroundServiceType Log file FileLogger is an actor (calls are awaited) FileLogger does blocking IO → call it inside withContext(Dispatchers.IO)

docs.title: 1. Requirement
docs.text:
The app can already listen to the peripheral (Read + Notify, task 003) but can't talk yet. This task adds 2 things:

  1. Write characteristic — send bytes to a characteristic with the WRITE or WRITE NO RESP property.
  2. The user picks the target characteristic, types the content as text (with the \r escape) or hex, previews the bytes, then taps Send.
  3. The main reason: the CarMD dongle (ELM327, UART port FFE0/FFE1) only returns data via notify after receiving a command such as ATZ\r. Without Write, enabling Notify on FFE1 shows nothing.
  4. MTU — know and display the connection's maximum packet size, block payloads over the limit.
  5. 🤖 Android requests MTU 247 itself after discovery (requestMtu, through the gattOps queue).
  6. 🍎 iOS has no API to request it — only reads the value iOS negotiated itself (maximumWriteValueLength).
  7. Why: the default MTU of 23 → each packet carries only 20 bytes of data; longer packets get truncated or rejected.

Source: README-HOW-TO-IMPLEMENT.md §8.4 (previously items 1 + 2 of the "After Day 4" list).

docs.title: 2. Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• AC1 — A characteristic with WRITE / WRITE NO RESP has a Write button; tapping it selects it as the write target. By default the app picks the write target itself (FFE1 → Nordic UART RX 6E400002-… → the first writable one), marked ★.
  • AC2 — The Write block has an input box + Text / Hex mode. Text: ATZ\r (type \r \n \t as escapes) → 41 54 5A 0D. Hex: 41 54 5A 0D, 41545A0D, 0x41,0x54 are all accepted. A preview of the bytes to send; invalid input → a red line, Send disabled.
  • AC3 — Tap Send → writes to the peripheral (with WRITE → with response, only NO RESP → without response); Received Data gets a line WRITE FFE1 41 54 5A 0D → "ATZ\r". Write errors (e.g. status=3 WRITE_NOT_PERMITTED) show in red.
  • AC4 — CarMD dongle: enable Notify FFE1 → Send ATZ\r → a NOTIFY reply line (ELM327 …) shows in Received Data.
  • AC5 — MTU: 🤖 after discovery requestMtu(247) through the queue; 🍎 reads maximumWriteValueLength(.withoutResponse) + 3. The GATT block shows MTU 247 · max 244 bytes per packet; payloads over the limit are blocked before sending. Disconnect → back to 23.
  • AC6 — Unit tests with the same cases 🤖🍎 for fromHex, fromText, planWrite, writeTargetOf, maxPayloadOf.

AC1–AC5 need a real device + a peripheral (nRF Connect GATT server, an ESP32 or a CMD-… dongle).

Out of scope: auto-reconnect + resubscribe · chunking payloads longer than the MTU · a flow-control queue for write-without-response (canSendWriteWithoutResponse / bursts of onCharacteristicWrite) · storing a history of sent commands · a separate Device detail screen.

                        └─ Ok(bytes, withResponse) → preview "41 54 5A 0D (4 bytes)"

     🤖 gattOps.enqueue ─► writeCharacteristic ─► onCharacteristicWrite ─► received += GattValue(WRITE)
     🍎 writeValue(.withResponse)    ─► didWriteValueFor ─► received += GattValue(WRITE)
        writeValue(.withoutResponse) ─► (no callback) ─► received += GattValue(WRITE) right away
 the peripheral answers ─► notify ─► received += GattValue(NOTIFY)   (already in Day 4)

      🍎 connect / discovery done ─► maximumWriteValueLength(.withoutResponse) + 3 ─► mtu
      disconnect ─► mtu = 23

docs.title: 4. Behaviour table (Day 14) — measured 2026-10-05
docs.text:
Devices: 🤖 Pixel 9 Pro emulator, Android 17 (API 37) · 🍎 iPhone 17 Pro Max Simulator, iOS 26.5. Data = lines in monitor.jsonl (the source column).

State 🤖 In-app loop 10 s 🤖 FGS 10 s 🤖 WorkManager 15′ 🍎 In-app loop 10 s 🍎 BGAppRefresh Foreground ✅ steady 10 s ✅ steady 10 s ✅ ENQUEUED, the first run fires right when scheduled (12:03:40) ✅ steady 10–11 s — (only runs in the background) Background (Home) ✅ kept writing for 70 s (11:36:41 → 11:37:49, process not frozen) — not guaranteed: Android may freeze/kill a cached process at any time ✅ 7 lines / 60 s, 10 s apart (11:31:16 → 11:32:17) ⏳ waiting for the 15′ schedule ❌ stops immediately: last line 11:52:58, Home at 11:53:01, 0 lines in 60 s (app suspended) ❌ Simulator: submit error BGTaskSchedulerErrorDomain error 1 · ⏳ real iPhone Return to foreground the loop is still running (same process) still running — ✅ resumes immediately (11:54:21), an 83 s gap in the log — OS termination (process killed) ❌ dead for good, doesn't restart (am kill 11:37:59 → 0 new lines); reopen = STOPPED, 0 records ✅ kill -9 11:32:32 → the system recreates the service after ~4 s (Scheduling restart of crashed service … 3826ms, restarted=true), writing again from 11:32:40. am kill can't kill it (an FGS process isn't cached) ✅ schedule survives (WorkManager keeps its own DB) ❌ simctl terminate: 0 lines; reopen = STOPPED ⏳ real device (Apple: can still be woken up) Force-kill ❌ ❌ am force-stop 11:33:02: service gone, no restart, 0 lines in 40 s ❌ schedule cancelled (the job disappears); reopening the app makes WorkManager reschedule (WM-ForceStopRunnable: Application was force-stopped, rescheduling) ❌ (= swiping it away in the App Switcher) ❌ swiped away → doesn't run until reopened (Apple docs) · ⏳ to measure Screen off / Doze 10′ ⏳ real device ⏳ (FGS is exempt from Doze for CPU, network may be blocked) ⏳ (Doze defers to a maintenance window) ⏳ ⏳ Reboot ❌ ❌ (doesn't auto-start — by design, no BOOT_COMPLETED added) ⏳ (WorkManager re-registers itself after boot) ❌ ⏳

Conclusions 1. A short, regular interval (10 s) while the app is in the background → only an Android Foreground Service can do it, at the cost of a notification. iOS has no equivalent; a few seconds in the background and the app is suspended. 2. Long periodic work (≥ 15′), timing drift acceptable → 🤖 WorkManager (survives OS kill + reboot) · 🍎 BGAppRefresh (iOS doesn't guarantee an interval, it may never run). 3. Force-kill is the user's decision: both platforms stop everything, there's no legitimate way to run again until the user opens the app — this app doesn't work around it. 4. The in-app loop on Android "seems" to keep running in the background on the emulator, but nothing keeps the process alive — don't rely on it.

Emulator notes: wifiConnected=false because the emulator's virtual Wi-Fi lacks NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED; the virtual Bluetooth stack (API 37) hung with HCI timeout during testing, making System UI and the app ANR on launch (main thread waiting on the Bluetooth binder) — an emulator bug, not caused by the Week 3 code.

docs.title: TASK — API client: two ways to connect (own URLSession code vs Alamofire)
docs.text: Platforms: iOS only · Created: 2026-10-12 · Builds on the Day 10 API tab

docs.title: 1. Requirement
docs.text:
• Keep the existing API features as they are: GET with params · POST JSON · default headers · HTTP error · timeout (8 s) · no network.
  • Split "how to connect" into two interchangeable backends behind one protocol:
  • Way 1, own code: URLSessionApiClient (Apple framework, no dependency).
  • Way 2, library: AlamofireApiClient (Alamofire 5 via SPM).
  • Add a segmented Picker on the API tab so you can run the same 6 presets through either backend and compare.
  • Branch with switch so the code is easy to read.
  • Out of scope: typed Codable models, interceptors/retry, and Android.

docs.title: 2. How the API tab runs: one tap, start to finish
docs.text:
ApiView (SwiftUI, @MainActor)
  │ @State backend: ApiBackend = .urlSession      ← the Picker writes this
  │
  │ tap "GET /status/500"
  ▼
 send(preset)
  ├─ sending = true · lastRequest = "[Alamofire] GET https://…"
  ├─ let client = backend.client ───────────────────────────── SWITCH 1: which way to connect
  │     ApiBackend.client
  │      switch self
  │       ├─ case .urlSession → URLSessionApiClient.shared
  │       └─ case .alamofire  → AlamofireApiClient.shared
  │
  └─ Task {
       switch preset.method ────────────────────────────────── SWITCH 2: which request
        ├─ case "POST" → await client.post(url, body:)
        └─ default     → await client.get(url, params:)
       sending = false
     }

 ── inside the chosen backend (runs off the main thread) ─────────────────────────────

 URLSessionApiClient                          AlamofireApiClient
  ApiHelpers.buildURL(url, params)             ApiHelpers.buildURL(url, params)      ← identical URL
  URLRequest + headers + timeout               session.request(url, method:, headers:,
  try await session.data(for:)                   requestModifier: timeout + body)
                                               await .serializingData().response
     │ got HTTPURLResponse?                       │ response.response != nil?
     ├─ yes → ApiHelpers.result(from:data:)       ├─ yes → ApiHelpers.result(from:data:)
     │         switch statusCode                  │         (read response.data — empty body is OK)
     │          ├─ 200...299 → .success           │
     │          └─ default   → .httpError         │
     └─ throws URLError                           └─ no → switch response.result
          → ApiHelpers.classify                          └─ .failure(AFError) → unwrap underlyingError
              switch e.code                                   → ApiHelpers.classify (same rule)
               ├─ .timedOut → .timeout
               ├─ offline/DNS/host → .noNetwork
               └─ default → .failure

 ── back in ApiView ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  result = ApiResult  →  ApiStrings.statusLine(result)  switch over 5 cases → green/red line + pretty JSON

The View only ever sees ApiResult. It never sees an Error, a URLSession, or Alamofire.

docs.title: 3. Files
docs.text: File Role ApiClient.swift protocol ApiClient { get · post } plus default arguments ApiResult.swift the 5-case result enum (moved here unchanged) ApiHelpers.swift pure shared rules: buildURL · classify · result(from:) · prettyJSON · default headers and timeout URLSessionApiClient.swift way 1, own code AlamofireApiClient.swift way 2, library ApiBackend.swift enum { urlSession, alamofire }; the one switch that picks the client ApiView.swift · ApiStrings.swift Picker plus switch preset.method project.yml packages: Alamofire from 5.10.0, resolved to 5.12.2 (Package.resolved committed)

docs.title: 4. URLSession vs Alamofire: what actually differs
docs.text: Topic URLSession (way 1) Alamofire (way 2) Dependency none SPM package Error style do / try / catch, throws URLError never throws here; response.result = .failure(AFError) that wraps the URLError HTTP 500 not an error, so check statusCode yourself same, as long as you don't call .validate(); .validate() turns 500 into AFError.responseValidationFailed Empty body (httpbin /status/500 = 0 bytes) data is just empty serializingData() fails with .inputDataNilOrZeroLength, so read response.data directly Query params built by hand has URLEncoding, but we pass the URL from buildURL so both send identical bytes Timeout URLRequest(timeoutInterval:) requestModifier { $0.timeoutInterval = … } Default headers only ours Session adds User-Agent / Accept-Language / Accept-Encoding; check with "GET headers echo" Testing fake URLProtocol the same fake URLProtocol via Session(configuration:)

Plus the switch picks the right client, an AFError-wrapped timeout classifies like URLSession, and the pure helper tests.
  • Real app on the iPhone 17 Pro Max Simulator with Alamofire selected: GET /status/500 gives HTTP ERROR · 500, and GET headers echo gives SUCCESS · HTTP 200.

docs.title: 6. Adding a 3rd way later
docs.text:
1. Add a new file XxxApiClient: ApiClient.
  2. Add a new case xxx in ApiBackend. The compiler then flags every switch that must handle it (label, client, backendHint, the test client(_:)).
  3. The tests run on it automatically through ApiBackend.allCases.

docs.title: TASK 007 — MVVM lesson 01: mini Pomodoro timer
docs.text: Platform: 🍎 iOS only (no Android twin yet) · Created: 2026-10-13 · Branch: feat/mini-pomodoro-timer Entry: Monitor tab → ⏱ button (top right). Launch straight into it: xcrun simctl launch booted com.learn.NativeDeviceMonitor -openPomodoro

docs.title: 1. Goal · scope · out of scope
docs.text:
Goal: learn MVVM the way Swift developers write it today — one small screen where:

  1. the View holds no logic (draws + forwards taps),
  2. the ViewModel is unit-tested without a screen and without waiting real time,
  3. the storage can change (UserDefaults → file → SwiftData) without touching View / ViewModel.

In scope: 25:00 focus → 05:00 break → focus…; Start / Pause / Resume, Reset, Skip; progress ring; "focus sessions today" kept in UserDefaults; time stays right after lock / background.

Out of scope (backlog §6): notifications, Live Activity, sound, custom durations, long break, history, Android.

docs.title: 2. Layers
docs.text:
PomodoroView (SwiftUI)            reads timeText · progress · phaseTitle · primaryTitle · todayText
   │ calls primaryTapped · reset · skip · tick · appBecameActive
   ▼
PomodoroViewModel                 @MainActor @Observable — import Observation, NOT SwiftUI
   │ init(store:, now:, calendar:)   ← dependencies come in from outside
   ▼
PomodoroEngine (NativeCore)       pure functions: (state, now) → new state
PomodoroSessionStore (protocol)   UserDefaultsPomodoroSessionStore · InMemoryPomodoroSessionStore (tests, #Preview)
File Layer NativeCore/Pomodoro/PomodoroEngine.swift Model: PomodoroPhase, PomodoroStatus, PomodoroState, PomodoroEngine NativeCore/Pomodoro/PomodoroSessionStore.swift Data: protocol + real + in-memory UI/Pomodoro/PomodoroViewModel.swift ViewModel UI/Pomodoro/PomodoroView.swift · ProgressRing.swift · PomodoroStrings.swift View UI/Monitor/MonitorView.swift owns the VM (@State) + pushes the screen — the timer survives going back NativeDeviceMonitorTests/PomodoroEngineTests.swift · PomodoroViewModelTests.swift 11 + 8 tests

docs.title: 3. The key idea — time
docs.text: Wrong: Timer every second doing remaining -= 1 → iOS suspends the app in the background, the counter freezes. Right: on Start store endDate = now + remaining; every tick remaining = endDate - now. now is passed in, so a test moves a fake clock by 25 minutes in one line. endDate lives inside .running(endDate:) — an idle/paused timer can't hold a stale one.

docs.title: 4. Steps (read the code in this order)
docs.text: # Read Ask yourself 1 PomodoroEngine.swift + PomodoroEngineTests Why is start a pure function and not a method that mutates? Which test fails if tick stamped now instead of endDate? 2 PomodoroSessionStore.swift What changes if we move to SwiftData? (answer: one new type + one line in MonitorView) 3 PomodoroViewModel.swift + PomodoroViewModelTests Why private(set)? Why is timeText in the VM and not in the View? 4 PomodoroView.swift Why .task(id: isRunning) and not Timer.publish? What cancels the loop? 5 MonitorView.swift (pomodoro, showPomodoro) Who creates the VM, and why not PomodoroView itself? 6 Exercise (yourself): copy the VM to an ObservableObject + @Published + @StateObject version, list the differences, delete it

docs.text:
Các trang "how to test": trên app bấm gì, phải thấy gì, thế nào là pass hay fail. Mỗi trang viết ngắn. Muốn xem code phía sau thì theo link sang tài liệu chi tiết.

# How to test Gồm 1 Tab Permissions Cấp / từ chối / từ chối vĩnh viễn, Open app settings, card Bluetooth radio, Ready to scan, Request all, test lại từ đầu 2 Luồng BLE (tab Scanner) Scan → Connect → Discover → Notify / Read / Write → Disconnect, kèm các lệnh dongle CarMD (ATZ\r, ATI\r, 010C\r)

Có tính năng mới sẽ thêm trang vào đây.

docs.title: 2 · BLE flow (Scanner)
docs.text: ← Test · BLE flow, từng file · Setup thiết bị test

docs.title: How to test · Luồng BLE (tab Scanner)
docs.text: Cầm điện thoại, làm theo trang này: mỗi bước BLE bắt buộc, trên màn hình hiện gì, bạn tự bấm hay app tự làm. Code phía sau từng bước: BLE flow, từng file · How to implement.

docs.title: 1. Tóm tắt flow
docs.text:
Bước yêu cầu Trên app Ai làm Scan Bấm Scan Bluetooth, sau 10 s tự dừng Bạn Chọn thiết bị Bấm vào 1 dòng trong Discovered Devices Bạn Connect Bấm Connect, status hiện Connecting… rồi Connected to X Bạn Discover services Connect xong app tự chạy discoverServices() Tự động Discover characteristics Có luôn trong kết quả discover; block GATT hiện N services · M characteristics Tự động Subscribe notification Bấm Notify trên dòng có ★ target (app ghi CCCD 2902) Bạn Nhận data Có dòng NOTIFY … trong Received Data Tự hiện Read data Bấm Read, có block Last read với raw: + value: Bạn Disconnect Bấm Disconnect: app tắt notify, ngắt kết nối, xoá block GATT Bạn (thêm) MTU Discover xong app tự xin MTU 247 (chỉ Android) Tự động (thêm) Write Gõ lệnh (hoặc bấm lệnh có sẵn), bấm Send Bạn 
Scan ─▶ Chọn ─▶ Connect ─▶ Discover services + characteristics ─▶ (MTU 247, Android)
                                        │
                                        ├─▶ Notify (CCCD 2902) ─▶ Received Data
                                        ├─▶ Read  ─▶ Last read
                                        └─▶ Write ─▶ (câu trả lời về qua Notify)
                                                                        │

docs.text:
• Tab Permissions: đã cấp BLE Scan + BLE Connect (xem How to test · Permissions).
  • Bluetooth đang bật. Tab Scanner hiện Ready to scan: YES, không phải card Not ready.
  • Có 1 thiết bị đang phát sóng ở gần. Chọn 1 trong 2:
    • Thiết bị test: điện thoại Android B chạy nRF Connect, có Battery Service 180F / 2A19 (READ + NOTIFY). Cách setup: Setup thiết bị test.
    • Dongle CarMD (ELM327, cổng UART FFE1): đã có điện (cắm vào xe hoặc cáp nguồn OBD).

docs.title: 3. Các bước test
docs.text: Mỗi dòng: Làm gì và Phải thấy gì. Không thấy đúng như cột Phải thấy = bước đó fail.

docs.title: A. Scan & connect
docs.text: # Làm Phải thấy 1 Mở tab Scanner, bấm Scan Bluetooth Nút đổi thành Stop scan; status Scanning… N found; các dòng hiện trong Discovered Devices kèm tên + -xx dBm 2 Đợi 10 s, không bấm gì Scan tự dừng, nút trở lại Scan Bluetooth 3 (Tuỳ chọn) bật CarMD tools only / gõ vào Device Name Danh sách được lọc (3 of 7); tắt lọc → Showing every BLE device 4 Bấm vào dòng thiết bị của bạn Dòng được chọn, nút Connect bấm được 5 Bấm Connect Status: Connecting… → Status: Connected to <tên>; dòng đó có nhãn CONNECTED

docs.title: B. Discover (tự động)
docs.text: # Làm Phải thấy 6 Không bấm gì, chỉ nhìn block GATT Discovering services… → N services · M characteristics; các dòng Read target:, Notify target:, Write target: có giá trị; 1 dòng có ★ target 7 Chỉ Android MTU 247 · max 244 bytes per packet (iOS không có dòng MTU)

docs.title: C. Notify, Read, Write
docs.text: # Làm Phải thấy 8 Bấm Notify trên dòng ★ target Nút đổi thành Stop 9 Thiết bị test: gửi 1 giá trị từ nRF Connect (máy B) Dòng hh:mm:ss.mmm NOTIFY 2A19 5A → 90 % trong Received Data, bộ đếm 1 / 50 10 Bấm Read Last read: 2A19 … với raw: 64 và value: 100 % (tuỳ giá trị máy B đang giữ) 11 Dongle CarMD: bấm lệnh có sẵn ATZ\r, rồi Send Dòng xem trước → 41 54 5A 0D (4 bytes); vài trăm ms sau có NOTIFY FFE1 … → "ELM327 v1.5" 12 Làm lại với ATI\r, rồi 010C\r (cắm xe, nổ máy) ATI → chuỗi version; 010C → trả về 41 0C .. (RPM), xem mục 5 13 Đổi ô nhập sang Hex, gõ 41 5 Chữ đổi đỏ, nút Send mờ (hex sai bị chặn) 14 Bấm Clear Received Data trống lại

docs.title: D. Disconnect
docs.text: # Làm Phải thấy 15 Bấm Disconnect Disconnecting… → Status: Disconnected; block GATT về lại Connect a device to list… 16 Đang kết nối thì tắt máy B / rút dongle Status tự về Disconnected, app không crash

docs.title: 4. Write có dư không? Write để Read phải không?
docs.text:
Không phải. Read và Write độc lập với nhau:

  • Read: app tự hỏi peripheral một giá trị có sẵn. Ví dụ pin 2A19 trả về 64 = 100 %. Read không cần Write trước.
  • Write: app gửi lệnh xuống. Câu trả lời về qua Notify, không về qua Read.
Peripheral Có cần Write không? Thiết bị test thường (nRF Connect, ESP32, đồng hồ…) Không. Write là phần dư so với flow yêu cầu Dongle CarMD (ELM327, cổng UART FFE1) Bắt buộc. Dongle không tự gửi gì, phải nhận lệnh mới trả lời. Bật Notify mà không Write = Received Data trống mãi

Thứ tự quan trọng với dongle: bật "tai" trước, rồi mới "nói".

Notify FFE1  ─▶  Write "ATZ\r"  (41 54 5A 0D)  ─▶  dongle trả "ELM327 v1.5" qua NOTIFY

docs.title: 5. Từng lệnh Write là gì
docs.text:
Dongle hiểu 2 loại lệnh:

  • Lệnh AT…: nói chuyện với chính con dongle (chip ELM327). Không cần cắm xe vẫn chạy.
  • Lệnh hex như 01 0C: là yêu cầu OBD-II, dongle chuyển tiếp tới ECU của xe. Phải cắm dongle vào xe và bật chìa khoá.
Lệnh Loại Làm gì Thường trả về Cần xe? ATZ\r AT (dongle) Reset dongle, giống khởi động lại. Nó trả về tên/version. Dùng đầu tiên để kiểm tra đường truyền thông chưa ELM327 v1.5 Không ATI\r AT (dongle) Hỏi version, không reset ELM327 v1.5 Không 010C\r OBD-II Mode 01 = "dữ liệu hiện tại", PID 0C = vòng tua máy (RPM) 41 0C 1A F8 → (0x1AF8) ÷ 4 = 1726 rpm Có
  • \r = carriage return (byte 0D), tức phím Enter. Dongle đợi ký tự này rồi mới chạy lệnh. Thiếu \r = không trả lời.
  • Ở chế độ Text bạn gõ thẳng \r, \n, \t, app tự đổi sang byte. Dòng xem trước cho thấy đúng các byte sẽ gửi.
  • Trong câu trả lời: 41 = "trả lời cho mode 01", tiếp theo là PID (0C), rồi tới các byte dữ liệu.
  • Trả về NO DATA hoặc ? = xe không hỗ trợ PID đó, hoặc gõ sai lệnh.

Đừng quên \r

Chữ \r (carriage return, 0D) ở cuối là bắt buộc. Thiếu là dongle không trả lời.
